transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Well... I suppose I'm here because of an ongoing situation at my apartment. It's been happening for months now. 

The property manager and... certain people in the building, they've been trying to pressure me out. It's just a constant stream of things. Misdelivered mail. Noises in the walls timed at very specific moments. Little comments from the neighbors when I walk by. 

They keep trying to hand me paperwork or offer these... explanations to cover it up. But it doesn't change the pattern. I can see exactly what they're doing.
Besides noticing these patterns and noises, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?
No. ... I don't hear voices. The noises I'm talking about are actual, physical sounds. Anyone standing in my apartment would hear them if they were paying attention.

Over these past few months, have you also noticed changes in your mood—like feeling unusually elevated, energetic, or irritable, or on the other hand, feeling very down, hopeless, or losing interest in things?
No. I haven't noticed anything like that. My mood is fine. I'm just... dealing with the situation at the apartment, that's all.

Before this situation with the apartment started, would you say you've generally had a hard time trusting people in general—like coworkers, family, or friends—throughout most of your life, or is this kind of suspicion new and specific to what's happening at your building?

No, not really. I've always gotten along fine with my coworkers. My family and I... we're fine. 

This is just about the building. It's... it's specific to them. They're the ones doing this. I don't just go around suspecting everyone I meet.
Do you have any chronic medical conditions, or have you been using any medications, recreational drugs, or alcohol around the time these experiences started?
No. I don't have any medical problems. And I don't use drugs. I might have a beer with dinner sometimes, but... no, nothing like that. I don't take anything.
Can you tell me exactly how many months ago you first started noticing these things happening at your apartment?
About... 11 months. It started shortly after I moved into the new place.

There are no hallucinations, no disorganized speech/behavior, and no negative symptoms, ruling out schizophrenia (functioning outside the delusional theme appears intact, with preserved relationships with coworkers and family). Mood symptoms (mania/depression) were explicitly denied, ruling out a mood disorder with psychotic features. The suspiciousness is circumscribed to the specific persecutory theme and not a lifelong pervasive distrust pattern, arguing against paranoid personality disorder. Substance use and medical causes were denied. The presentation—an isolated, well-systematized delusion without other psychotic or mood symptoms, present for more than 1 month—is most consistent with Delusional Disorder (F22).
